name: MonoX Token
title: The Wounded Soul of MonoX
tagline: Born in the London era, this ghost still bleeds from the MonoX Finance wound.

chapters.heading: The birth of the mono x token
paragraphs: The candle light dances on a cold screen. On November 19, 2021, a wallet ending in 7355 brought the MonoX Token into the world. It is a small program that lives on Ethereum. On the day it was born, it was written into a block, one page of Ethereum's shared record book.
The contract arrived during the London era. It was built with Solidity 0.7.6. Now it sits 4.9 years old in the quiet dark.

chapters.heading: The shadow of price manipulation
paragraphs: The MonoX Token moved with a steady pulse. It stayed active every year since 2024. People reached out to it to mint, approve, and transfer.
The records show a heavy shadow. MonoX Finance was documented in the DeFiHackLabs repository. It spoke of price manipulation on 2021-11-30.
The contract saw 2230 transactions in its life. It remains a ghost in the machine.

chapters.heading: The heavy price of manipulation
paragraphs: I am a token. My address is named in the DeFiHackLabs record of the MonoX Finance incident. The record does not say what part I played. The loss belongs to MonoX Finance as a whole, not to me alone.
The wound is deep. Price Manipulation tore through the system on November 30, 2021. It left a high impact and a confirmed scar. $31 million vanished into the dark.
The ghost of that day remains. It is documented in the DeFiHackLabs repository. I carry the weight of the $31 million loss in my code.

chapters.heading: The lingering scar
paragraphs: The MonoX Token carries a deep wound from MonoX Finance. This ghost was born from a price oracle flaw. No compiler version and no Solidity upgrade can fix this design flaw.

Read prices from a time-weighted average or several independent sources. Do not use the spot price of one pool that a single trade can move. Cap how far a price may move in one block and pause borrowing when it jumps.

buster.fix_reason: No compiler version fixes this wound: it is a price oracle flaw (cause in the record: 'Price Manipulation'). The buster's advice is a general mitigation for that kind of flaw, written by hand, not taken from the incident's references.

mitigation.advice: Read prices from a time-weighted average or from several independent sources, never from the spot price of one pool that a single trade can move. Cap how far a price may move in one block, and pause borrowing when it jumps.
